title: Sell Mineral Rights in Missouri
metaTitle: Sell Gas Royalties in Missouri | Forest City Basin Owners
metaDescription: Own a small legacy gas interest in northwest Missouri's Forest City basin edge? We give honest, written offers on modest Missouri gas royalties.
heroLead: the gas royalty desk has bought interests all over gas country, and the gas royalty desk will tell you plainly that Missouri isn't one of the big ones — but that doesn't mean what you're holding is worthless, just that it needs an honest look instead of a big sales pitch.
intro: Northwest Missouri sits on the eastern edge of the Forest City basin, a shallow, thin formation that extends mostly into Kansas and Nebraska, with only a modest sliver reaching into Missouri counties like Atchison, Nodaway, and Holt. Coalbed methane and shallow conventional gas production has happened out there over the years, but it's always been small-scale compared to the basin's more active acreage further west, and drilling activity in the Missouri portion has never really taken off the way it did across the state line.

If you hold an interest in this part of the state, chances are you're looking at a modest, low-volume legacy well rather than anything resembling the major plays this site talks about in Louisiana or Arkansas. That's fine. Plenty of small, honest interests are still worth selling — they just need to be priced like what they are.

sections.heading: Why the Forest City basin never took off in Missouri
paragraphs: The basin thins out heading east into Missouri, and the coal seams and shallow gas-bearing zones that made the Kansas and Nebraska portions worth developing more aggressively get less favorable on this side of the line. Operators generally chased the better rock further west, which left Missouri's slice of the play with a scattering of modest wells rather than a real development boom, and that pattern has held steady for as long as the play has been understood.

That history matters for expectations: if a landman or another buyer tells you your Missouri interest is sitting on the next big gas play, be skeptical. The geology here has been understood for a long time, and it's never pointed toward a major buildout. We'd rather set that expectation honestly up front than have you wait years for activity that isn't coming.

sections.heading: What a modest Missouri interest looks like day to day
paragraphs: Checks tend to be small and can be irregular, since these are low-volume wells operated by smaller companies that may not prioritize this acreage the way a major operator would prioritize a core shale asset. Production reporting can also be less consistent than what you'd get from a larger operator with better back-office systems, which sometimes makes it harder for an owner to track exactly what's happening with their well from month to month.

None of that means the interest has no value — it means the honest value is modest, and a lump-sum sale can be genuinely more useful to an owner than years of small, hard-to-track checks from a well that was never going to be a major producer. For a lot of owners, trading that uncertainty for a known number now is worth more than the theoretical future total of the checks.

sections.heading: How we approach a small Missouri interest
paragraphs: We ask for whatever statements or division order paperwork you have, even if it's thin, and we do the legwork of tracking down production records through the state and county if your own paperwork is incomplete. Given how modest these interests typically are, we try to keep the process simple rather than making you jump through the same hoops we might use on a major Haynesville or Piceance transaction.

If, after we look at everything, the honest answer is that your interest doesn't carry much value, we'll say so rather than string you along. Most owners appreciate a straight answer over a runaround, even when the number isn't exciting, and that's true whether the interest is a Forest City sliver or a major Haynesville unit.

faqs.question: Is northwest Missouri a real natural gas play?
faqs.answer: It's a minor edge of the Forest City basin, with modest, scattered production. It's never developed into a major play the way the Kansas and Nebraska portions of the basin have.

faqs.question: Why is your Missouri gas check so small and irregular?
faqs.answer: These are typically low-volume wells run by smaller operators, sometimes with less consistent reporting than a major company would provide, which can make checks both modest and harder to predict month to month.

faqs.question: Is it worth selling a small Missouri gas interest?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if you'd rather have a lump sum than years of small, irregular checks from a well that was never going to be a major producer. We price it honestly rather than oversell what it is.

faqs.question: What if you do not have complete paperwork on your interest?
faqs.answer: We can track down production and ownership records through the state and county if what you have is incomplete, so missing paperwork isn't a dealbreaker.

faqs.question: Should you expect much drilling activity near your Missouri tract?
faqs.answer: Probably not. The Missouri edge of the Forest City basin has never seen the development pace of the Kansas and Nebraska portions, and there's little reason to expect that to change based on the geology involved.
